hero.subtitle: Where innovation leads and technology accelerates: we manage your project from start to finish and deliver photorealistic renders in minutes, not weeks.
hero.videoAlt: The architectural process: from drawing to 3D model, from render to built work

method.title: Structured architecture. Instant visualization.
method.body: Behind every render is a technical model — detailed and designed to be built. AI doesn't create the architecture; it takes that 100% human design and projects it into a photorealistic visualization. Drag to discover each project's frame in both states.
method.sliderLabel: Comparison between 3D model and final render

speed.title: Agile decisions, solid architecture
speed.body: The real value of a project lies in how it's conceived and structured. That's why we automate the visual process, cutting timelines from weeks to minutes so decisions get made with agility and certainty. We reinvest that time where it matters most: refining constructive details, driving innovation and functionality, and above all, making sure the design becomes reality with absolute precision.

cards.label: Time per image
cards.note: The render stops being a milestone on the schedule and becomes part of the conversation — and a tool for decision-making.

cards.label: Visual iterations per project
cards.note: Exploring new design alternatives no longer changes the delivery timeline.

cards.label: When you decide
cards.note: Clients approve and make final decisions from the very first images created for the project, with no need for other exploration tools.

work.title: {count} views. From model to matter.
work.body: See the technical model and the final visualization. Click any of them to see the before and after in detail.

services.title: From the first line to the last delivery.
services.body: The render is the way in, not the destination. LARQA covers the complete project — and can also step in at just the stage you need.

items.title: AI visualization
items.description: Photorealistic exterior, interior and detail renders, produced in minutes and directed by architectural judgement.

items.title: 3D modeling
items.description: Building the model from drawings, sketches or references. The foundation every image rests on.

items.title: Architectural design
items.description: The complete project: brief, massing, layout and technical resolution. From idea to buildable drawing.

items.title: Interior design
items.description: Materials, lighting and furniture defined as one coherent system, not as a collection of pieces.

items.title: Technical documentation
items.description: Plans, sections, elevations and specifications ready for permitting and for site.

items.title: Project direction
items.description: Support from start to finish so that what gets built is exactly what was designed.

steps.title: Brief
steps.description: We define the brief, references and scope. You leave this stage knowing exactly what you'll receive and when.

steps.title: Model
steps.description: We build the massing in 3D from your drawings or from a new design. This is where the architecture gets decided.

steps.title: Render
steps.description: AI produces the image in minutes. We review framing, light and materiality, and adjust until it's the right image.

steps.title: Delivery
steps.description: You get high-resolution files, ready for sales, permitting or publication. And if the project continues, so do we.

about.name: Laura Martínez
about.lead: AI generates images. Deciding which of them is architecture is still an architect's job.
about.body1: Laura runs LARQA on a simple conviction: the tool doesn't replace judgement. A render is only useful if the light falls where it should, if the material behaves the way it would on site, and if the plan behind the image actually works.
about.body2: That's why every project starts in the model, not in the prompt. Speed comes from the technology, but the decisions — the framing, the proportion, the detail that makes a space feel livable — come from the craft.
about.quote: AI gave me back the time I used to spend waiting. Now that time goes into the project.
